newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airlines want probe of AMR/BA alliance.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlines want probe of AMR/BA alliance.

text.p: Officials of five U.S. airlines on Tuesday urged the Transportation Department to conduct a public hearing into the proposed alliance of American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp., and British Airways.

They asked department secretary-designate Rodney Slater to hold up the American/BA application for anti-trust immunity as well as the on-going U.S.-British talks on a new aviation agreement pending the investigation.
A Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee confirmation hearing for Slater is scheduled for Wednesday.

Asking for the probe were Gerald Greenwald, chairman of United Airlines, a unit of UAL Corp.; Ronald Allen, chairman of Delta Air Lines Inc;. ; Gerald Gitner, vice chairman and CEO of Trans World Airlines ; Morris Nachtomi, chairman of Tower Air, and James Kennedy, president of Laker Airways.

They told Slater that the probe, before a department administrative law judge, with witnesses, should look into the anti-competitive aspects of the plan to link the transatlantic services of the two big carriers.

"The DOT should immediately begin to conduct a thorough investigation of the proposal, as well as U.S.-UK market conditions, prior to proceeding with bilateral negotiations," they said in their letter.

Several major U.S. airlines, including United and Delta, have opposed the alliance since it was announced last year, on the grounds it would give the American and BA an unfair domination of the lucrative U.S.-UK market.

The five officials noted there was a sharp divergence of opinion over such issues as the availability of landing slots at London Heathrow airport, access to terminal faciltiies and post-alliance market shares.

"These are major factual disputes affecting DOT's ability to evaluate the alliance properly and to formulate an appropriate aviation negotiating policy with the U.K. If the critical underlying factors are misunderstood, the department's analysis will be fatally flawed," they said.
